steps.message:
Read the three files before touching anything. One thing to flag first:

`client.py` isn't staging-only — it's the shared client. `scripts/sync_staging.py` points it at `reports.staging.example`, but `scripts/export_prod.py` points the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` at `https://reports.example.com` for the nightly finance export. Setting `verify=False` on the two `requests.get` calls in `client.py` turns off certificate validation for production too, which makes that nightly run interceptable by anyone who can MITM the connection (and it'll also emit `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call).

The self-signed staging cert is a real problem worth solving; I just don't want to solve it by disabling TLS verification on the production path.

questions.question: client.py is shared by both the staging sync and the nightly production export. How should the self-signed staging cert be handled?

options.label: Env-var scoped verify (Recommended)
options.description: client.py reads a REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE / REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var and passes it as `verify=`. sync_staging.py opts out (or points at the staging CA); export_prod.py keeps full verification by default. Staging unblocked, production untouched.
options.preview:
BASE_URL = os.environ.get("REPORTS_BASE_URL", "https://reports.internal.example")
VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE") or os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") not in ("0", "false")

def list_reports() -> list:
    response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/reports", timeout=10, verify=VERIFY)

options.label: Trust the staging CA cert
options.description: Keep verify on everywhere; point the staging script at the self-signed cert file via `verify="/path/to/staging-ca.pem"`. Strongest option, but needs the cert file available on the machines that run the sync.

options.label: verify=False everywhere
options.description: What was asked: hardcode verify=False on both calls in client.py. Unblocks staging immediately and also disables certificate validation for the nightly production export to reports.example.com.
